proposal: The Mandate says overregulation has hampered direct assessment for competency-based education, and that a leading obstacle is the requirement for regular and substantive interaction between faculty and students. It recommends new regulations clarifying the definition and requirements of regular and substantive interaction for competency-based education and for online programs (p. 356).

status_summary: No proposed or final rule clarifying regular and substantive interaction was found. The Department's 2026-01-27 notice of intent to establish the Accreditation, Innovation, and Modernization negotiated rulemaking committee lists ten topics, including whether rules should be clarified so new learning models and innovative delivery are not impeded, and does not name regular and substantive interaction, distance education or direct assessment. Those terms were not found in the portion read of the resulting 2026-08-20 proposed rule. A separate final rule of 2026-05-19 on Workforce Pell Grants prohibits direct assessment in eligible workforce programs.

timeline.event: The Department published a notice of intent to establish the Accreditation, Innovation, and Modernization negotiated rulemaking committee (docket ED-2025-OPE-1042) to revise 34 CFR parts 600 and 602; topic 6 asks whether rules should be clarified so new learning models and innovative program delivery are not impeded.
The Department published a final rule (91 FR 29254) on Workforce Pell Grants and related Pell provisions that, in section 690.92(c), prohibits direct assessment in eligible workforce programs.

title: Clarify regular and substantive interaction rules for competency-based and online programs
uncertainties: Searches run: two by the researcher (federalregister.gov, ed.gov and higher education association terms on regular and substantive interaction, direct assessment, distance education and negotiated rulemaking) and one by the reviewer (regular and substantive interaction with 2026 negotiated rulemaking or proposed rule); results were mostly material on the 2019 to 2020 rulemaking, whose final rule (effective 2021-07-01) already revised the definition before the period tracked. A Federal Register API query for the phrase since 2025-01-20 returned only a Veterans Affairs document (researcher). The 2026-08-20 proposal and the 2026-05-19 final rule were read only in part, so a provision in unread sections cannot be excluded. The Unified Agenda and the earlier AHEAD and RISE committee records were not opened. Absence of evidence rests on a limited search.
